trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any trade-deal headline (USTR, METI, White House) coincides with the probability move; confirm EWJ and Nikkei futures tick direction.
time_plan.1h: Compare EWJ move vs SPY/ACWI to isolate Japan-specific vs broad risk beta; watch USD/JPY.
time_plan.2h: Reassess if move is holding or fading; check Japanese auto/machinery names (TM, Nikkei exporters) for confirmation.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against Tokyo cash session open reaction and any official statements.
time_plan.12h: Mark final EWJ return vs expectation; note whether the probability shift was news-driven or noise, and whether it was already public.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a US-Japan trade agreement becoming law signals reduced tariff risk and improved market access for Japanese exporters, which is broadly supportive of Japanese equities. EWJ is the most liquid, diversified US-listed proxy for the Japanese market and captures this exporter/trade sentiment. However, the resolution bar here (an FTA becoming US law via ratification or Congressional-Executive Agreement before end-2026) is high and slow-moving; a probability move is unlikely to translate into a large same-day equity move.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether USD/JPY reacts at all to the probability move.
time_plan.1h: Separate rate-driven (UST/JGB yields) from trade-driven yen moves.
time_plan.2h: Check if BoJ or MOF commentary is interfering with the signal.
time_plan.6h: Reassess against broader dollar index (DXY) to avoid attributing dollar moves to the trade headline.
time_plan.12h: Mark final FXY move; most likely conclude the mapping was weak/noisy.

predictions.reasoning: A trade deal's FX impact is ambiguous: reduced trade friction could support the yen via improved Japanese export outlook, but risk-on sentiment typically weakens the yen as a funding/safe-haven currency. These offset, so direction is genuinely unclear and the signal is weak. FXY is the liquid US-listed yen proxy but exposure to this specific catalyst is tenuous.

evidence_used: Market question: US-Japan trade deal becoming US law before 2027
High legal resolution bar (ratification or Congressional-Executive Agreement signed into law)
Japan's export-driven economy and sensitivity to US tariff/trade policy
EWJ and FXY as the most liquid US-listed Japan proxies
uncertainty_notes: A probability shift in a multi-year legislative market rarely produces a large same-day move in broad equity ETFs.
Trade-deal news may already be public and priced, making any anomaly stale.
FX direction is theoretically ambiguous (risk-on yen weakness vs export-supportive yen strength).

llm_justification.summary: A sharp rise in the implied probability of a US-Japan trade agreement becoming law would modestly favor Japanese equities (EWJ up) on reduced tariff risk, while the yen (FXY) direction is genuinely ambiguous. Both mappings are weak over a 12h horizon because the market resolves on a slow, high-bar legislative outcome; expected moves fall well short of the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is a low-confidence, non-tradable research signal.
key_assumptions: A probability move reflects genuine new information about trade-deal prospects rather than noise or liquidity.
EWJ meaningfully captures Japan-specific trade sentiment on a same-day basis.
No offsetting macro/monetary shock dominates the tape during the window.
failure_modes: The trade-deal development is already public and fully priced, so no asset move follows.
Broad risk-on/risk-off or dollar moves swamp the Japan-specific signal, misattributing the cause.
The proxies (EWJ, FXY) are only weakly exposed to a slow legislative outcome, producing noise below the 700bps threshold.
The probability move reverses as the headline is clarified or denied.
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
